Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

reference noun

a recommendation for a job

also letter of recommendation, give someone a reference, recommend someone, testimonial

classical

Cic. Fam. 13.20.1: meamque commendātiōnem ūsuī magnō sibi fuisse
Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: ego enim renovābō commendātiōnem

commendātiō, commendātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a recommendation, a reference

The thirteenth book of Cicero’s letters to his friends is almost all references of this kind.

Other words

  • commendō, commendāre, commendāvī, commendātum — recommend (someone to someone)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.20.1: hunc igitur tibi commendō · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • 1commendātīcius: long i in -īcius (Lewis & Short commendātĭcĭus). Adjectives in -īcius made from perfect participles have a long ī, and Lewis & Short marks it so in ēmptīcius, conductīcius, missīcius, trālātīcius, adventīcius; only its commendātĭcĭus and collātĭcĭus stand apart.

    litterae commendātīciae1 — a letter of recommendation

    litterae, litterārum f. pl., with the adjective commendātīcius, -a, -um · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.5.1: nūllās ad tē litterās mittere nisi commendātīciās

Examples

  • hunc igitur tibi commendō et ā tē petō ut dēs operam ut intellegat dīligenter mē scrīpsisse dē sēsē meamque commendātiōnem ūsuī magnō sibi fuisse

    So I recommend him to you, and ask you to see to it that he understands I wrote about him with care and that my reference did him a great deal of goodCic. Fam. 13.20.1

  • etsī statueram nūllās ad tē litterās mittere nisi commendātīciās1

    although I had decided to send you no letters but letters of recommendationCic. Fam. 5.5.1

See also interview, position, job.
